newsitem.title: USA: Mobil says return of Calif. unit unknown.
newsitem.headline: Mobil says return of Calif. unit unknown.

text.p: Mobil Corp officials said on Friday they had not determined when they would restart a unit damaged in an early morning fire at the Torrance, Calif. refinery.
The fire started when gasoline leaked from a pump in the refinery's PTR unit. The PTR, or platform reforming unit, helps turn low grade gasoline into high grade product.
Firefighters contained the fire less than two hours after it erupted.
"It was a leaking pump ignited by something," said spokeswoman Carolin Keith, adding the cause of the ignition remained unknown.
Traders said earlier this week that another unit, the fluid cataltyic cracker (FCC), was resuming service Friday.
When asked if the FCC's return caused the fire, spokeswoman Carolin Keith said: "This morning's fire probably had nothing to do with any other unit."
She declined to confirm if the FCC had returned.
The refinery processes 130,000 barrels per day of crude oil and makes 1.5 billion gallons of gasoline every year.
Separately, Keith said modifications of the plant's hydrogen flouride unit will begin in mid-September.
"The modifications to the unit are part of an agreement we have with the city (of Torrance) to begin using modified hydrogen flouride," Keith said.
The modifications will allow operators to make a form of hydrogen flouride much easier to clean up with water, Keith said.
"We are hoping to commission the unit in May or June," she said.
